title: 哈姆雷特 3-2 戲中戲
style_suffix: black and white ink comic style, high contrast, heavy shadows, cold gothic atmosphere
characters: Hamlet, a lean young prince dressed head to toe in black, a short dark cloak, tousled dark hair, pale clean-shaven face with shadowed sleepless eyes

panels.prompt: backstage behind a makeshift stage curtain, {characters} instructing a group of costumed players, miming a measured gesture with one raised hand, masks and prop crowns hanging around them

dialogue.speaker: 哈姆雷特
dialogue.text: 唸台詞要唸得順口自然。要是像有些伶人那樣張牙舞爪，我寧願叫街上的宣令員來唸——一切不要過火。
dialogue.en: Speak the speech, I pray you, as I pronounced it to you, trippingly on the tongue: but if you mouth it... I had as lief the town-crier spoke my lines... o'erstep not the modesty of nature.

panels.prompt: two-shot in a shadowed alcove, {characters} gripping the shoulder of Horatio, a sober young scholar in a plain dark scholar's gown with a high collar, short neatly combed brown hair, a small leather book at his belt, both glancing toward the lit hall beyond

dialogue.speaker: 哈姆雷特
dialogue.text: 今晚有一場戲，其中一段情節很像我父親的死。好霍拉旭——替我盯緊我的叔父。
dialogue.en: There is a play to-night before the king; one scene of it comes near the circumstance which I have told thee of my father's death... Observe mine uncle... Give him heedful note.

panels.prompt: the great hall arranged as a theatre, torches blazing, King Claudius, a broad heavyset king with a neatly trimmed dark pointed beard, a wide gold crown, fur-trimmed brocade robes, a jeweled goblet in hand, and Queen Gertrude, a stately middle-aged queen with coiled auburn braids under a golden circlet, in a layered brocade gown, enthroned among courtiers, {characters} sprawled deliberately at the feet of Ophelia, a slight young woman with very long loose fair hair, wide gentle eyes, in a simple pale flowing gown

dialogue.speaker: 哈姆雷特
dialogue.text: 好極了——跟變色龍一樣吃空氣過活，塞滿了諾言。
dialogue.en: Excellent, i' faith; of the chameleon's dish: I eat the air, promise-crammed.

panels.prompt: the little stage seen past silhouetted audience heads, mime players performing a dumb-show: a crowned figure asleep on a bank of prop flowers, a cloaked figure tipping a vial into his ear

dialogue.speaker: 旁白
dialogue.text: 啞劇開場——一個人，往睡著的國王耳中，倒進毒藥。
dialogue.en: The dumb-show enters: a man pours poison into the sleeping king's ear.

panels.prompt: on a small wooden stage with painted canvas scenery, lit from below by a row of candle footlights, a Player Queen in a paste crown kneels clasping exaggerated vows over the reclining Player King, seen past the dark silhouetted heads of the front-row audience

dialogue.speaker: 伶后
dialogue.text: 要是我死了丈夫再作新人，讓詛咒永遠跟隨我！
dialogue.en: In second husband let me be accurst! None wed the second but who kill'd the first.

panels.prompt: {characters} twisting around from the floor to look up at Queen Gertrude, a stately middle-aged queen with coiled auburn braids under a golden circlet, in a layered brocade gown, whose fan has stopped moving, her smile frozen

dialogue.speaker: 哈姆雷特
dialogue.text: 母親，您覺得這齣戲怎樣？
dialogue.en: Madam, how like you this play?

dialogue.speaker: 葛簇特
dialogue.text: 我想那位夫人發的誓，太重了些。
dialogue.en: The lady doth protest too much, methinks.

quote.text: 那位夫人發的誓太重了
quote.en: The lady doth protest too much, methinks.

panels.prompt: the play within the play: on the candle-lit wooden stage a sinister player in black tips poison into the sleeping Player King's ear, framed by painted scenery and watched past silhouetted courtiers' heads, while in the near foreground {characters} leans far out of his seat, lips parted, eyes locked on the royal box

dialogue.speaker: 哈姆雷特
dialogue.text: 他在花園裡毒死了他，篡奪了他的位置。這故事是真事改編——瞧著吧，兇手馬上就要得到王后的愛了。
dialogue.en: He poisons him i' the garden for's estate... the story is extant, and writ in choice Italian: you shall see anon how the murderer gets the love of Gonzago's wife.

panels.prompt: KING CLAUDIUS surging up from his seat, the jeweled goblet crashing from his hand, courtiers recoiling, torch flames streaming sideways, his broad face lit from below in raw terror
chaos of scattering courtiers and streaking torches emptying the hall, benches overturned, while two figures stand still against the flow — the black-clad prince and the scholar in his dark gown

dialogue.speaker: 哈姆雷特
dialogue.text: 好霍拉旭！那鬼魂的話，一個字也不假——一千鎊我也敢賭。你看見了嗎？
dialogue.en: O good Horatio, I'll take the ghost's word for a thousand pound. Didst perceive?

panels.prompt: close-up of Horatio, a sober young scholar in a plain dark scholar's gown with a high collar, short neatly combed brown hair, a small leather book at his belt, nodding once, grim and certain, an abandoned torch guttering on the floor behind him

dialogue.speaker: 霍拉旭
dialogue.en: Very well, my lord... I did very well note him.

panels.prompt: Rosencrantz, a plump smooth-faced courtier with a short blond bowl-cut and an eager ingratiating smile, and Guildenstern, a thin courtier with lank dark hair and nervous darting eyes, cornering {characters} in a corridor, the prince thrusting a wooden recorder flute into the thin courtier's reluctant hands

dialogue.speaker: 哈姆雷特
dialogue.text: 你願意吹吹這管笛子嗎？
dialogue.en: Will you play upon this pipe?

panels.prompt: extreme close-up of the prince's pale face gone cold and quiet, the recorder held up between two fingers like evidence, torchlight edging his shadowed sleepless eyes

dialogue.speaker: 哈姆雷特
dialogue.text: 你們把我當作什麼樂器？隨便你們把我叫作什麼樂器——你們可以撥弄我，卻不能玩弄我。
dialogue.en: Why, look you now, how unworthy a thing you make of me! You would play upon me... call me what instrument you will, though you can fret me, yet you cannot play upon me.

quote.text: 你們可以撥弄我，卻不能玩弄我
quote.en: Though you can fret me, yet you cannot play upon me.

panels.prompt: very wide shot of {characters} walking alone down a pitch-black corridor toward a distant lit doorway, his shadow thrown long behind him, one hand resting on the dagger at his belt

dialogue.speaker: 哈姆雷特
dialogue.text: 現在是深夜的巫魅時刻，墳墓洞開，地獄向人間吐出瘟疫。……我要去見我的母親了。心啊，不要失去你的天性——我要用利劍一樣的說話，可是決不用劍。
dialogue.en: Tis now the very witching time of night, when churchyards yawn and hell itself breathes out contagion to this world... Soft! now to my mother... I will speak daggers to her, but use none.

quote.text: 用利劍一樣的說話，可是決不用劍
quote.en: I will speak daggers to her, but use none.
